question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Autumn leaves shuffled beneath him as he wandered through the quiet forest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. rustled underfoot.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "shuffled" (of dry leaves) suggests a soft, dragging, crackling sound made as they are moved by the feet. "Rustled underfoot" — meaning made a light crackling sound when stepped on — best captures this sense and keeps the sentence natural and vivid. (पैरों तले सरसराना)

◦ Correct: Autumn leaves rustled underfoot as he wandered through the quiet forest.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "crushed around" is unnatural and awkward in this context.

• Option 3 "moved to another place" changes the meaning (leaves are not relocating).

• Option 4 "died over" is not a valid English expression.

NOTE

• "Rustle" = to make a soft, light sound like that of dry leaves or paper moving. "Underfoot" = under one's feet, on the ground where one is walking.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The ___________ of the novel kept me hooked from the beginning to the end.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. plot.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "plot" of a novel is the sequence of events / the main storyline that holds a reader's interest. A gripping plot "keeps one hooked from beginning to end". (कथानक)

◦ Correct: The plot of the novel kept me hooked from the beginning to the end.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "archaic" (an adjective meaning very old / out of date) cannot follow "The ___ of the novel".

• Option 2 "settlement" (a place where people settle / an agreement) does not fit.

• Option 3 "orchestra" (a large group of musicians) is unrelated to a novel.

NOTE

• Literary terms: plot (storyline), theme (central idea), protagonist (main character), narrator (one who tells the story), climax (turning point).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

His artwork is / more intricate / than any artist / in the gallery.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. than any artist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The comparison is illogical/incomplete. We are comparing his artwork with an artist, which is not a like-for-like comparison. It should be "than that of any other artist" (comparing artwork with artwork). Hence the segment "than any artist" carries the error.

◦ Correct: His artwork is more intricate than that of any other artist in the gallery.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• When comparing two things of the same class, both must be of the same kind (artwork vs artwork, not artwork vs artist).

• Also, with "any", the word "other" is required so that the subject is not compared with itself.

NOTE

• Rule of parallel comparison: use "that of / those of" to compare possessions — "His salary is higher than that of his colleague" (not "than his colleague").

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Appease
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Pacify.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Appease" means to calm, soothe or satisfy someone (often by giving in to demands). Its closest synonym is "pacify" (to make peaceful/calm). (शांत करना / मनाना)

◦ Example: The manager tried to appease/pacify the angry customers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Aggravate" (to worsen / annoy) is an antonym.

• Option 2 "Force" (to compel) and Option 4 "Appeal" (a request / to attract) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of appease: pacify, placate, mollify, soothe, conciliate. Antonyms: aggravate, provoke, irritate, inflame.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

They worked / very hardly / on their project / for several weeks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. very hardly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hard" is itself an adverb meaning "with great effort" (work hard). "Hardly" is a different adverb meaning "scarcely / almost not". So "worked very hardly" is wrong — it should be "worked very hard".

◦ Correct: They worked very hard on their project for several weeks.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "hardly" would give the opposite, illogical meaning — "they scarcely worked".

• "for several weeks" (duration) and "on their project" are grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Confusing adverb pairs: hard (with effort) vs hardly (scarcely); late (not early) vs lately (recently); near (close) vs nearly (almost).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and complete the given idiom.

That's great! You keep everything under your _________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. thumb.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to keep/have (someone or something) under one's thumb" means to keep under one's control or influence. (अपने नियंत्रण/वश में रखना)

◦ Correct: That's great! You keep everything under your thumb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "eyes", "legs" and "hands" do not form the standard idiom here; only "under your thumb" carries the sense of control.

NOTE

• Related "thumb" idioms: "rule of thumb" (a rough practical guideline), "thumbs up/down" (approval/disapproval), "green thumb" (skill at gardening).

question:
Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank and make the sentence meaningful.

Before retiring, Kaul had been teaching physics at the university for three __________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. decades.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "decade" is a period of ten years. "Three decades" (thirty years) fits a long teaching career before retirement, and it is the correctly spelt, meaningful word. (दशक)

◦ Correct: ... had been teaching physics at the university for three decades.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "decimals" (numbers with a decimal point) is unrelated to time.

• Option 3 "decadents" (people in moral decline) does not fit.

• Option 4 "edecamals" is not an English word.

NOTE

• Time periods: decade (10 years), score (20 years), century (100 years), millennium (1000 years).

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Poverty is the urgent concern in India today.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. most urgent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" before an adjective naming a single, foremost concern signals the superlative degree. As "urgent" is a longer adjective, its superlative is "most urgent".

◦ Correct: Poverty is the most urgent concern in India today.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "urgenter" and 2 "urgentest" are wrong forms — longer adjectives never take "-er/-est".

• Option 3 "more urgent" is comparative (used with "than"), not suitable with "the ... concern".

NOTE

• Degrees of "urgent": urgent – more urgent (comparative, with "than") – the most urgent (superlative, with "the").

question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error.

He has / no / influence about / me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. influence about.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The noun "influence" takes the preposition "over" or "on", not "about". So it should be "influence over me".

◦ Correct: He has no influence over me.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "He has", "no" and "me." are all correct in the sentence.

NOTE

• Correct collocations: "influence over/on someone", "an influence on his decision", "under the influence of". "Influence about" is incorrect.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Persevrence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Persevrence" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "perseverance", meaning continued steady effort/persistence despite difficulty. (दृढ़ता / लगन)

◦ Spelling key: PER + SE + VER + ANCE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The other options are correctly spelt: "conscientiousness" (the quality of being careful and diligent), "accommodate" (to provide room / adjust) and "exaggerate" (to overstate).

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt words to remember: accommodate (double c, double m), exaggerate (double g), perseverance (no "r" before "ance" other than the shown one — per-se-ver-ance).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The land that is best suitable for growing crops
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Arable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Arable" means (land) suitable or used for growing crops / for ploughing. (कृषि योग्य भूमि)

◦ Example: The fertile plains of Punjab are highly arable land.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Barren" (unable to produce crops/vegetation) is the opposite.

• Option 3 "Fruitful" (productive, in a general sense) and Option 4 "Rustic" (rural / simple, of the countryside) do not precisely mean cultivable land.

NOTE

• Related terms: arable land (crop-growing), pasture (grazing land), fallow (left unsown to recover fertility), fertile (rich, productive).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Benevolent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Malevolent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Benevolent" means kind, generous and well-wishing. Its direct antonym is "malevolent", meaning wishing evil or harm to others. (परोपकारी का विलोम — द्वेषपूर्ण)

◦ Example: A benevolent ruler cares for his people; a malevolent one harms them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Eminent" (famous/distinguished), Option 3 "Violent" (using force) and Option 4 "Opulent" (rich/luxurious) are unrelated.

NOTE

• The Latin roots "bene-" (good) and "male-" (bad/evil) give many opposite pairs: benevolent/malevolent, benefactor/malefactor, benediction/malediction.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I am not going to pay a ________ for this broken CD.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. cent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "cent" is a small unit of money (a hundredth of a dollar). "Not going to pay a cent" is an idiomatic way of saying "not going to pay even the smallest amount". (एक पैसा भी नहीं)

◦ Correct: I am not going to pay a cent for this broken CD.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "scent" (a pleasant smell/perfume) is a homophone but wrong in meaning.

• Option 3 "sent" (past tense of send) and Option 4 "send" (verb) are grammatically wrong here.

NOTE

• Homophones: cent (coin) / scent (smell) / sent (past of send). Similar money idioms: "not worth a penny", "won't pay a dime".

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Manoj has a bigger / farmhouse of one hundred / hectares near the city.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Manoj has a bigger.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The comparative "bigger" is used without any comparison ("than ..."). Here no comparison is intended, so the positive degree "big" (or "a big") should be used. Hence the segment "Manoj has a bigger" carries the error.

◦ Correct: Manoj has a big farmhouse of one hundred hectares near the city.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "farmhouse of one hundred" and "hectares near the city." are correct.

• A comparative adjective ("bigger", "larger") needs an implied or stated object of comparison; with none, use the positive degree.

NOTE

• Use the comparative only when two things are compared ("bigger than yours"); use the positive degree to describe a single thing ("a big house").

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

My hands are full
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To be very busy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "one's hands are full" (to have one's hands full) means to be very busy / fully occupied with work. (बहुत व्यस्त होना)

◦ Example: With three young children, she really has her hands full.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 (to dislike someone), 3 (to panic) and 4 (to go directly towards something) do not match the meaning of this idiom.

NOTE

• Related "hand" idioms: "hand in glove" (in close cooperation), "a free hand" (full freedom to act), "out of hand" (out of control), "at hand" (near/available).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Whim
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Fancy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "whim" is a sudden, passing wish or fancy without any particular reason. Its closest synonym is "fancy" (a sudden liking or impulse). (सनक / मौज)

◦ Example: On a whim/fancy, she booked a flight to the hills.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Antiquity" (ancient times), Option 2 "Factualness" (being factual) and Option 3 "Bloodiness" are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of whim: fancy, impulse, caprice, urge, notion. "Whimsical" = acting on sudden fancies; playfully unpredictable.

question:
Select the most appropriate word segment that can replace the underlined part in the sentence.

The two thieves divided the looted money with themselves.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. between themselves.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When something is shared by two persons, we use "between". As there are exactly "two thieves", the money is divided "between themselves".

◦ Correct: The two thieves divided the looted money between themselves.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "with themselves" is incorrect for sharing.

• "among themselves" (Option 1) is used for more than two — here there are only two thieves, so "between" is right.

• "of themselves" and "off themselves" are ungrammatical here.

NOTE

• Rule: "between" for two; "among" for more than two. "Divide the sweets between the two boys" / "among the five boys".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Secresy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Secresy" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "secrecy", meaning the state of being secret / keeping things hidden. (गोपनीयता)

◦ Spelling key: SEC + RE + CY.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The other options are correctly spelt: "hypocrisy" (pretending to have virtues one lacks), "cruelly" (in a cruel manner) and "luggage" (bags/suitcases).

NOTE

• Nouns ending in "-cy": secrecy, privacy, accuracy, diplomacy, literacy. Note "secrecy" (not "secresy").

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The water near the coast was shallower and clean.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. shallow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective is joined by "and" to "clean", which is in the positive degree. To keep the two adjectives parallel, "shallower" (comparative) should also be positive — "shallow". Also, no comparison ("than") is present.

◦ Correct: The water near the coast was shallow and clean.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "shallowest" and 2 "the shallowest" are superlatives (need "the ... of all"); Option 4 "more shallow" is comparative (needs "than") — none fits alongside "clean".

NOTE

• When two adjectives describe the same noun and are joined by "and", keep them in the same degree: "shallow and clean" (both positive).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Destroy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Ruin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Destroy" means to damage completely / to demolish or wreck. Its closest synonym is "ruin" (to spoil or damage severely). (नष्ट करना / बर्बाद करना)

◦ Example: The flood destroyed/ruined hundreds of homes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Delight" (great pleasure), Option 3 "Decline" (to refuse / to decrease) and Option 4 "Fabricate" (to make up / to construct) do not mean the same as destroy.

NOTE

• Synonyms of destroy: ruin, demolish, devastate, wreck, annihilate, raze. Antonyms: build, create, construct, repair.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The eye of an ostrich is larger than its brain. Of all birds, ostriches have the 1.________ eyes. Their eyes are the size of a pool ball, measuring around 2 inches in diameter. Their size is five times greater than that of human eyes. Ostriches have excellent vision, so their enormous eyes aren't just for show. Because of their height and keen 2.________, the birds can see well over great distances, enabling them to identify potential 3._________ before they approach. In general, compared to mammals of comparable size, birds often have smaller brains. Ostrich brains are approximately 1.5 inches in width, the study found. Additionally, their average brain weight is almost 17 times lower than that of the three other 4._____. When comparing the brain-to-body weight ratio of the other birds, the ostrich's brain was lighter than their body weight. Some other facts concerning these birds are what set them apart. All other birds have three or four toes; this magnificent creature has only two. Ostriches bend their knees in a forward orientation; thus, they kick forward rather than backward. Furthermore, ostriches do not require water because they produce some of it internally and obtain the 5._______ from the plants they consume.

Select the most appropriate option for blank 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. biggest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "Of all birds" indicates a comparison among the whole group, which requires the superlative degree. The superlative of "big" is "biggest".

◦ Correct: Of all birds, ostriches have the biggest eyes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "bigger" is comparative (used with "than"); Option 3 "more big" is a wrong form (short adjectives take "-est", never "more"); Option 4 "big" (positive) does not suit "Of all birds".

NOTE

• Degrees of "big": big – bigger (than) – the biggest (of all). Superlative is signalled by "of all / in the world / the ... est".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The eye of an ostrich is larger than its brain. Of all birds, ostriches have the 1.________ eyes. Their eyes are the size of a pool ball, measuring around 2 inches in diameter. Their size is five times greater than that of human eyes. Ostriches have excellent vision, so their enormous eyes aren't just for show. Because of their height and keen 2.________, the birds can see well over great distances, enabling them to identify potential 3._________ before they approach. In general, compared to mammals of comparable size, birds often have smaller brains. Ostrich brains are approximately 1.5 inches in width, the study found. Additionally, their average brain weight is almost 17 times lower than that of the three other 4._____. When comparing the brain-to-body weight ratio of the other birds, the ostrich's brain was lighter than their body weight. Some other facts concerning these birds are what set them apart. All other birds have three or four toes; this magnificent creature has only two. Ostriches bend their knees in a forward orientation; thus, they kick forward rather than backward. Furthermore, ostriches do not require water because they produce some of it internally and obtain the 5._______ from the plants they consume.

Select the most appropriate option for blank 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. vision.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage says ostriches have "excellent vision" and can "see well over great distances", so their "keen vision" (sharp eyesight) lets them spot things far away. "Vision" means the power of seeing. (दृष्टि)

◦ Correct: Because of their height and keen vision, the birds can see well over great distances.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "delusion" (a false belief), Option 3 "illusion" (a false impression) and Option 4 "allusion" (an indirect reference) all concern something false or indirect, not eyesight.

NOTE

• Distinguish: vision (eyesight), illusion (a deceptive appearance), delusion (a false fixed belief), allusion (an implied/indirect reference).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The eye of an ostrich is larger than its brain. Of all birds, ostriches have the 1.________ eyes. Their eyes are the size of a pool ball, measuring around 2 inches in diameter. Their size is five times greater than that of human eyes. Ostriches have excellent vision, so their enormous eyes aren't just for show. Because of their height and keen 2.________, the birds can see well over great distances, enabling them to identify potential 3._________ before they approach. In general, compared to mammals of comparable size, birds often have smaller brains. Ostrich brains are approximately 1.5 inches in width, the study found. Additionally, their average brain weight is almost 17 times lower than that of the three other 4._____. When comparing the brain-to-body weight ratio of the other birds, the ostrich's brain was lighter than their body weight. Some other facts concerning these birds are what set them apart. All other birds have three or four toes; this magnificent creature has only two. Ostriches bend their knees in a forward orientation; thus, they kick forward rather than backward. Furthermore, ostriches do not require water because they produce some of it internally and obtain the 5._______ from the plants they consume.

Select the most appropriate option for blank 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. predators.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sharp vision from a height would help ostriches spot danger approaching. "Predators" (animals that hunt and eat other animals) is what a prey animal like the ostrich would need to "identify ... before they approach". (शिकारी जंतु)

◦ Correct: ... enabling them to identify potential predators before they approach.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "quarry" here means "prey that is hunted" — the ostrich is the hunted, not the hunter, so it does not fit.

• Option 2 "tours" (journeys) is irrelevant; Option 4 "victims" would be those already harmed, not the threat approaching.

NOTE

• In ecology, a predator hunts; its prey is hunted. Ostriches, being prey, watch out for predators such as lions, hyenas and cheetahs.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The eye of an ostrich is larger than its brain. Of all birds, ostriches have the 1.________ eyes. Their eyes are the size of a pool ball, measuring around 2 inches in diameter. Their size is five times greater than that of human eyes. Ostriches have excellent vision, so their enormous eyes aren't just for show. Because of their height and keen 2.________, the birds can see well over great distances, enabling them to identify potential 3._________ before they approach. In general, compared to mammals of comparable size, birds often have smaller brains. Ostrich brains are approximately 1.5 inches in width, the study found. Additionally, their average brain weight is almost 17 times lower than that of the three other 4._____. When comparing the brain-to-body weight ratio of the other birds, the ostrich's brain was lighter than their body weight. Some other facts concerning these birds are what set them apart. All other birds have three or four toes; this magnificent creature has only two. Ostriches bend their knees in a forward orientation; thus, they kick forward rather than backward. Furthermore, ostriches do not require water because they produce some of it internally and obtain the 5._______ from the plants they consume.

Select the most appropriate option for blank 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. species.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The comparison is of the ostrich's brain weight with that of "the three other species" of birds studied. "Species" means a group of similar organisms (here, other kinds of birds). (जाति / प्रजाति)

◦ Correct: ... their average brain weight is almost 17 times lower than that of the three other species.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "property" (a quality/possession), Option 3 "case" (an instance) and Option 4 "typical" (an adjective, not a noun) do not fit "the three other ___".

NOTE

• "Species" is both singular and plural (one species / many species). It is the basic unit of biological classification.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The eye of an ostrich is larger than its brain. Of all birds, ostriches have the 1.________ eyes. Their eyes are the size of a pool ball, measuring around 2 inches in diameter. Their size is five times greater than that of human eyes. Ostriches have excellent vision, so their enormous eyes aren't just for show. Because of their height and keen 2.________, the birds can see well over great distances, enabling them to identify potential 3._________ before they approach. In general, compared to mammals of comparable size, birds often have smaller brains. Ostrich brains are approximately 1.5 inches in width, the study found. Additionally, their average brain weight is almost 17 times lower than that of the three other 4._____. When comparing the brain-to-body weight ratio of the other birds, the ostrich's brain was lighter than their body weight. Some other facts concerning these birds are what set them apart. All other birds have three or four toes; this magnificent creature has only two. Ostriches bend their knees in a forward orientation; thus, they kick forward rather than backward. Furthermore, ostriches do not require water because they produce some of it internally and obtain the 5._______ from the plants they consume.

Select the most appropriate option for blank 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. remainder.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ostriches "produce some of it (water) internally and obtain the remainder from the plants they consume". "Remainder" means the rest / the remaining part. It logically completes the idea — some water is made internally, the rest comes from plants. (शेष भाग)

◦ Correct: ... they produce some of it internally and obtain the remainder from the plants they consume.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "each", 2 "every" (used with singular countable nouns) and 3 "lesser" (comparative adjective) do not fit "obtain the ___ from the plants".

NOTE

• "Remainder" = the part that is left over. Synonyms: rest, remnant, balance, residue. "Some ... the remainder" is a common paired construction.

question: The concept of the Self-Help Group Bank Linkage Program was introduced by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is NABARD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Self-Help Group (SHG) – Bank Linkage Programme" was introduced by NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) in 1992. It links informal self-help groups of the rural poor with formal banks for credit. (नाबार्ड — 1992)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It is the largest microfinance programme in the world in terms of client outreach.

• NABARD was established on 12 July 1982 as the apex bank for agriculture and rural development.

NOTE

• A Self-Help Group (SHG) is a small voluntary association (usually 10–20 members, often women) that pools savings and provides micro-loans to members.

question: In which year did India host the FIFA U 17 Women's Football World Cup?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2022.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India hosted the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in 2022 (October). Matches were held in Bhubaneswar, Margao (Goa) and Navi Mumbai. (2022)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Spain won the 2022 title by defeating Colombia in the final.

• Earlier, India also hosted the FIFA U-17 (Men's) World Cup in 2017.

NOTE

• Football's world governing body is FIFA (Fédération Internationale de Football Association), founded in 1904, headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland.

question: Which famous monument of Vijayapura has a Whispering Gallery, where subtle sounds can be heard clearly even from a distance of 37 metres?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gol Gumbaz.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Gol Gumbaz" at Vijayapura (Bijapur), Karnataka is famous for its "Whispering Gallery", where even faint sounds echo clearly across the dome. It is the mausoleum of Mohammed Adil Shah of the Adil Shahi dynasty. (गोल गुम्बज)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Gol Gumbaz has the second largest dome in the world (after St. Peter's Basilica, Rome).

• It was built in 1656 and is a fine example of Deccan/Indo-Islamic architecture.

NOTE

• The word "Gol Gumbaz" means "circular/round dome". Its acoustics make a whisper audible many times over across the gallery.

question: ___________ was an Indian mandolinist who was a master composer of the Carnatic style of classical music.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uppalapu Srinivas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Uppalapu Srinivas (U. Srinivas) was the legendary Indian mandolin player and a master exponent/composer of Carnatic classical music. He popularised the electric mandolin in Carnatic music. (यू. श्रीनिवास — मैंडोलिन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• He was popularly called the "Mandolin Srinivas" and was awarded the Padma Shri.

• Carnatic music is the classical music tradition of South India.

NOTE

• Other Carnatic greats: Kunnakudi Vaidyanathan (violin), M. S. Subbulakshmi (vocal), and the Carnatic "Trinity" — Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri.

question: In which of the following dance performance is the main percussion instrument Edakka used?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniattam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Edakka (Idakka), an hourglass-shaped drum of Kerala, is the main percussion instrument used in "Mohiniyattam", the classical dance of Kerala. (मोहिनीअट्टम — इडक्का)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Mohiniyattam ("dance of the enchantress, Mohini") is a graceful, feminine classical dance form of Kerala.

• The Edakka/Idakka is also used in temple music and to accompany Kathakali.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: The Government of India in collaboration with ___________ has launched the Skills on Wheels mission in Oct 2023 for equipping rural youth with employable skills.
solution_text:
The correct answer is IndusInd Bank.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Skills on Wheels" mission was launched in October 2023 by the Government of India in collaboration with IndusInd Bank, to equip rural youth with employable skills through mobile skilling units. (स्किल्स ऑन व्हील्स — इंडसइंड बैंक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The initiative uses mobile vans/buses to take vocational training to remote and rural areas.

• It supports the government's broader Skill India Mission and the goal of a skilled workforce.

NOTE

• Skill India Mission (launched 2015) is run by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE); PMKVY is its flagship scheme.

question: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award is given for the spectacular and most outstanding performance in the field of sports by a sportsperson over a period of the previous four years. In 2021, the awardee for para shooting was:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Avani Lekhara.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Avani Lekhara, the para shooter, received the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in 2021. She won gold in the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics (10 m air rifle), becoming the first Indian woman to win a Paralympic gold. (अवनि लेखरा — पैरा शूटिंग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (renamed in 2021 from the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna) is India's highest sporting honour.

• Neeraj Chopra (javelin) and Mirabai Chanu (weightlifting) were also 2021 awardees.

NOTE

• Major Dhyan Chand was the legendary Indian hockey player known as "The Wizard"; National Sports Day is celebrated on 29 August, his birthday.

question: Who appointed the 'Hunter Commission' for Educational Reforms in 1882?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Ripon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Hunter Commission" (Indian Education Commission) was appointed in 1882 by the Viceroy Lord Ripon, under the chairmanship of Sir William Wilson Hunter, to review the progress of education, especially primary education. (हंटर आयोग — लॉर्ड रिपन, 1882)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Lord Ripon (Viceroy 1880–84) is famous for the Ripon Resolution (1882) on local self-government — he is called the "Father of Local Self-Government in India". He also repealed the Vernacular Press Act.

• The Hunter Commission stressed the state's role in expanding primary and secondary education.

NOTE

• The Ilbert Bill controversy (1883) also occurred during Lord Ripon's tenure.

question: What is the tenure of a Governor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A Governor of a state holds office for a term of 5 years, but actually holds office during the pleasure of the President (Article 156). So the Governor can be removed earlier or continue beyond 5 years until a successor takes charge. (राज्यपाल का कार्यकाल — 5 वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Governor is appointed by the President (Article 155) and is the constitutional head of a state.

• Minimum age to be a Governor is 35 years (Article 157).

NOTE

• Articles related to the Governor: 153 (Governors of States), 154 (executive power), 155 (appointment), 156 (term), 161 (pardoning power).

question:
Which of the following statements is/are true about the Cholas?
1 The capital of the Chola kingdom was Tanjore.
2 Vikram Chola had in his veins the blood of the Cholas and Eastern Chalukyas.
3 Rajendra I Chola is known as Gangaikonda Chola.
solution_text:
The correct answer is All 1, 2 and 3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All three statements about the Cholas are correct:

◦ 1 — The capital of the Chola kingdom was Tanjore (Thanjavur).

◦ 2 — Vikrama Chola descended from both the Cholas and the Eastern Chalukyas (through the Chalukya-Chola line).

◦ 3 — Rajendra I Chola took the title "Gangaikonda Chola" ("conqueror of the Ganga") and founded the city Gangaikonda Cholapuram.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Chola dynasty was a powerful South Indian empire; Rajaraja I built the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur.

• Rajendra I extended Chola power up to the Ganga and across the seas to Srivijaya (Southeast Asia).

NOTE

• The Cholas are famous for their naval power, local self-government (village assemblies like Ur and Sabha) and magnificent Dravidian temple architecture.

question: How many artists are selected for the one-time Sangeet Natak Akademi Amrit Award, 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 86.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A total of 86 artists were selected for the one-time "Sangeet Natak Akademi Amrit Award", 2022. It was instituted to honour artists aged above 75 who had not received the Akademi Award, as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav. (संगीत नाटक अकादमी अमृत पुरस्कार — 86 कलाकार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's national academy for music, dance and drama, established in 1952; it is headquartered in New Delhi.

• The Amrit Award carried a purse and a citation, given for lifetime contribution to the performing arts.

NOTE

• Other national academies: Sahitya Akademi (literature) and Lalit Kala Akademi (fine arts), all set up in the 1950s.

question: Which of the following sessions of the Indian National Congress was headed by Sarojini Naidu?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanpur, 1925.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sarojini Naidu presided over the Kanpur session of the Indian National Congress in 1925, becoming the first Indian woman to be President of the INC. (सरोजिनी नायडू — कानपुर अधिवेशन, 1925)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sarojini Naidu, called the "Nightingale of India (Bharat Kokila)", was a poet and freedom fighter; she later became the first woman Governor of an Indian state (United Provinces).

• The first woman President of the INC overall was Annie Besant (1917, Calcutta); Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President.

NOTE

• Key sessions: Lahore 1929 (Purna Swaraj, J. L. Nehru), Karachi 1931 (Fundamental Rights, Sardar Patel), Madras 1927 (Independence resolution).

question: Which local storm is also known as 'Kalbaisakhi'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nor Westers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kalbaisakhi" is the local name (in West Bengal) for the violent pre-monsoon thunderstorms known in English as "Nor'westers" (as they come from the north-west). They occur in April–May. (कालबैसाखी — नॉर्वेस्टर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Kalbaisakhi" literally means "the calamity of the month of Baisakh".

• These storms bring heavy rain, thunder and squalls, and are beneficial for jute, tea and rice cultivation.

NOTE

• Other local storms/winds: Loo (hot dry summer wind of North India), Mango shower (pre-monsoon rain in Kerala/Karnataka), Bardoichila (storms in Assam).

question: Which festival is celebrated as the birth anniversary of Prophet Muhammad?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Milad-un-nabi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Milad-un-Nabi" (also called Eid-e-Milad or Mawlid) is celebrated as the birth anniversary of Prophet Muhammad. It falls in the Islamic month of Rabi' al-awwal. (मिलाद-उन-नबी — पैगंबर मुहम्मद का जन्मदिन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Eid-ul-Fitr marks the end of the fasting month of Ramadan.

• Id-ul-Zuha (Bakrid/Eid-al-Adha) commemorates the sacrifice of Prophet Ibrahim.

• Shab-i-Barat is the "night of forgiveness".

NOTE

• The Islamic calendar (Hijri) is lunar, so these festivals shift by about 10–11 days each year relative to the Gregorian calendar.

question: Which substance is commonly added to tap water to make it safe for drinking by killing harmful microorganisms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chlorine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chlorine" is commonly added to tap/drinking water (chlorination) because it kills harmful bacteria, viruses and other microorganisms, making the water safe to drink. (क्लोरीन — जल का शुद्धिकरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Chlorine is a strong disinfectant; bleaching powder (calcium hypochlorite) is also used for the same purpose.

• Excess chlorine can give a slight taste/odour, so the dose is carefully controlled.

NOTE

• Fluoride is sometimes added to prevent tooth decay, but in excess causes fluorosis. Chlorine is the standard disinfectant for public water supply.

question: Which of the following sectors engaged the largest percentage of women workers in the year 2019-2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agriculture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2019-2020, the "Agriculture" sector engaged the largest percentage of women workers in India. A very high share of rural working women are employed in farming and allied activities. (कृषि क्षेत्र — सर्वाधिक महिला श्रमिक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Agriculture remains the largest employer in India overall, and its share of women workers is especially high.

• Data on employment come from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by the NSO.

NOTE

• The three broad sectors of the economy: primary (agriculture), secondary (industry/manufacturing) and tertiary (services).

question: Which region in India has the highest concentration of Iron and Steel Industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chotanagpur plateau.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Chotanagpur Plateau" (spread over Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal and Chhattisgarh) has the highest concentration of the iron and steel industry in India, due to abundant iron ore, coal, manganese and cheap labour. (छोटानागपुर पठार — लौह-इस्पात उद्योग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Major steel plants here include Jamshedpur (TISCO), Bokaro, Durgapur, Rourkela and Burnpur.

• The Chotanagpur Plateau is called the "Ruhr of India" for its mineral wealth.

NOTE

• Iron and steel is a basic/heavy industry; the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) manages many public-sector steel plants.

question: During the framing of the Indian Constitution, the Constituent Assembly held a total of eleven sessions, with sittings spread over for how many days?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 165.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Constituent Assembly took about 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to frame the Constitution, holding 11 sessions spread over 165 days. (संविधान सभा — 11 सत्र, 165 दिन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Constituent Assembly was set up under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946); its first meeting was on 9 December 1946.

• Its first (temporary) President was Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha; the permanent President was Dr. Rajendra Prasad. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

NOTE

• The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950 (celebrated as Republic Day).

question: The title of the autobiography of famous cricketer of Pakistan Imran Khan is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is All Round View.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "All Round View" is the autobiography of the famous Pakistani cricketer (and former Prime Minister) Imran Khan. (इमरान खान की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Imran Khan captained Pakistan to victory in the 1992 Cricket World Cup and later became the Prime Minister of Pakistan (2018–2022).

• He also wrote another book titled "Pakistan: A Personal History".

NOTE

• Some cricket autobiographies: Playing It My Way (Sachin Tendulkar), A Century Is Not Enough (Sourav Ganguly), The Test of My Life (Yuvraj Singh).

question: Why will a person weigh more at the north or south pole?
option_1: Due to Earth's distance from the sun
option_2: Due to variation in centrifugal force of earth with latitude
option_3: Due to variation in centripetal force of earth with altitude
option_4: Due to variation in centripetal force of earth with latitude
solution_text:
The correct answer is Due to variation in centrifugal force of earth with latitude.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A person weighs more at the poles because the centrifugal force due to Earth's rotation varies with latitude — it is maximum at the equator and zero at the poles. At the poles there is no centrifugal force reducing weight, and the Earth's radius is smallest there, so g (and hence weight) is greatest. (ध्रुवों पर भार अधिक — अपकेंद्री बल शून्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Earth is an oblate spheroid — bulging at the equator and flattened at the poles. Smaller radius at the poles means stronger gravity.

• Weight = mass × g. Mass stays the same everywhere; only g (and thus weight) changes.

NOTE

• Value of g is about 9.83 m/s² at the poles and 9.78 m/s² at the equator — a person therefore weighs slightly more at the poles.

question: For most of the ecosystem, what is the primary source of energy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sunlight.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• For most ecosystems, the primary (ultimate) source of energy is "Sunlight". Green plants (producers) trap solar energy through photosynthesis and convert it into chemical energy (food), which then flows through the food chain. (सूर्य का प्रकाश — ऊर्जा का प्राथमिक स्रोत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The flow of energy in an ecosystem is unidirectional: Sun → Producers → Herbivores → Carnivores.

• Energy transfer follows the 10% law (only about 10% passes to the next trophic level).

NOTE

• Producers (autotrophs) make their own food using sunlight; consumers (heterotrophs) depend on others; decomposers recycle nutrients. Some deep-sea ecosystems instead use chemosynthesis (geothermal).

question: Which poet composed the Allahabad Prashasti of Samudragupta?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harisena.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Allahabad Prashasti (Prayag Prashasti)", which glorifies the conquests of the Gupta king Samudragupta, was composed by his court poet Harisena. It is engraved on an Ashokan pillar at Prayagraj (Allahabad). (प्रयाग प्रशस्ति — हरिषेण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Harisena was the court poet, minister and military officer of Samudragupta.

• The inscription is in Sanskrit and in the Champu style (mix of prose and verse). Samudragupta is called the "Napoleon of India" (by historian V. A. Smith).

NOTE

• Other famous prashastis/poets: Banabhatta wrote Harshacharita (on Harshavardhana); Vatsabhatti composed the Mandsaur inscription.

question: Which Indian state's cabinet approved the proposal for recommending the inclusion of the Kui language in the eighth schedule in July 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In July 2023, the Odisha state cabinet approved the proposal to recommend the inclusion of the "Kui language" in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution. Kui is spoken mainly by the Kandha (Kondh) tribe of Odisha. (ओडिशा — कुई भाषा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Eighth Schedule currently contains 22 languages.

• Languages are added to the Eighth Schedule by a constitutional amendment; the last additions were Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali (2003).

NOTE

• Being in the Eighth Schedule gives a language official recognition and eligibility for development grants and representation on the Official Languages Commission.

question: According to the census of India 2011, which union territory of India has the highest literacy rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lakshadweep.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, "Lakshadweep" had the highest literacy rate among the Union Territories, at about 91.8%. (लक्षद्वीप — सर्वाधिक साक्षरता वाला केंद्रशासित प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Among all states/UTs, Kerala had the highest literacy rate (94%); Bihar had the lowest.

• India's overall literacy rate in 2011 was about 74.04%.

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years; the 2011 Census was the 15th national census, with the theme "Our Census, Our Future".

question: In which of the following types of regions, is the maximum temperature variation observed between a day and the same night?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Desert.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In "desert" regions, the maximum temperature variation (diurnal range) between day and night is observed. Sand heats up quickly and cools quickly, and the dry air with little moisture/cloud cover cannot retain heat — so days are very hot and nights very cold. (मरुस्थल — दिन-रात के तापमान में सर्वाधिक अंतर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Coastal areas and islands have a small daily temperature range because water heats and cools slowly (high specific heat), keeping temperatures moderate.

• The difference between day and night temperatures is called the diurnal range of temperature.

NOTE

• Land heats/cools faster than water — this is why interiors and deserts have extreme (continental) climates, while coasts have equable (maritime) climates.
